invariants_the_new_contract_encodes: SINGLE ACTIVE CHARACTER — only the named speaker is present in the current scene. Other characters may be referenced as history, relationships, or future intentions ("If this gets weird, I'll call Rivet") but must NOT become active participants ("I call for Rivet. We line up a reprint...") — direct fix for §11 finding.

SINGLE PRESENT MOMENT — the script depicts one bounded scene happening now. Plans stay plans; describing an experiment's outcome inside the same script is forbidden unless current-scene evidence establishes completion.
PLANS REMAIN PLANS — establishing intent is fine; simulating multi-phase outcomes is not.
MEMORY AS BACKGROUND — retrieved NarrativeMemory rows are context the character already knows; they are NOT commands to reenact past events on-camera.
END ON A MOMENT — the scene finishes on a decision, reaction, hook, or landed observation — never a lesson-summary or process-summary.
PRESERVE CREATIVE FREEDOM — character voice, humor, opinions, tangents all remain; the constraints above are about scene physics, not tone.
section_f_writing_contract_seam.not_shared: _INVARIANTS_BLOCK + _NARRATIVE_SHAPES_BLOCK (the long-form narrative-shape menu promotes 'story → realization / mistake → lesson / experiment → outcome', which is exactly what causes temporal compression per §11.6). solo_scene emits its own scene-oriented menu with 'moment → reaction', 'discovery → intent', 'observation → resolve-or-defer', 'internal turn → decision'.

section_g_smallest_coherent_slice.scope_boundary: One coherent slice covers BOTH (a) SPA Episode-solo mode UX and (b) backend solo_scene writing contract — because splitting them would ship a half-mode: hiding fields without fixing the contract still produces §11-style scene drift; fixing the contract without hiding fields still exposes the wrong UX to the operator.
